# SnapDOM: v3 reference

SnapDOM is a browser capture engine for web interfaces.

It captures a DOM subtree, its computed styles and its assets into a reusable result. The core exports SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP, canvas and blobs, and reports capture geometry. Plugins add HTML, text or JSON context, annotated element maps, image-based PDFs and recordings.

SnapDOM has two integrated render engines: `svg` (default) and experimental `html-in-canvas`. Both receive the same finished clone; the second uses the browser's native painter and falls back to SVG when unavailable or unsuitable for the capture.

Package: `@zumer/snapdom`. License: MIT. Source: https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom. Documentation: https://snapdom.dev/docs/.

This reference describes the v3 prerelease checkout. The npm and CDN commands below install the published release, which may differ from this API. To try v3, run `npm install` and `npm run compile` inside its checkout. Release details: https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom#installation.

## Installation

```bash
npm install @zumer/snapdom
```

```js
import { snapdom } from '@zumer/snapdom';
```

For a browser script tag, use the IIFE build, which exposes `window.snapdom`:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@zumer/snapdom/dist/snapdom.js"></script>
```

For a browser ES module:

```html
<script type="module">
  import { snapdom } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@zumer/snapdom/dist/snapdom.mjs';
</script>
```

The package entry is ESM; there is no CommonJS build. The core has no runtime dependencies. Official plugins are a separate package:

```bash
npm install @zumer/snapdom-plugins
```

```js
import { htmlExport, contextExport, agentMap } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';
```

The core registry subpath uses the same runtime as the package root:

```js
import { registerPlugins, clearPlugins, getGlobalPlugins } from '@zumer/snapdom/plugins';
```

## Capture once, export several ways

```js
const capture = await snapdom(document.querySelector('#card'));
const png = await capture.toPng({ width: 1200, dpr: 1 });
const svgBlob = await capture.toBlob();
await capture.download({ format: 'jpg', filename: 'card.jpg' });
document.body.appendChild(png);
```

These exports use the captured state, even if the live element changes later. Call `snapdom(element)` again to capture those changes. Eligible repeated captures may reuse an unchanged result or update a changed subtree.

Recording plugins are an explicit exception: `toGif()` and `toMp4()` take new frames from the live element when the export starts.

## Core API

```text
snapdom(element, options?)          → Promise<CaptureResult>
snapdom.fromString(html, options?)  → Promise<CaptureResult>
snapdom.toRaw(element, options?)    → Promise<string>
snapdom.toSvg(element, options?)    → Promise<HTMLImageElement>
snapdom.toPng(element, options?)    → Promise<HTMLImageElement>
snapdom.toJpg(element, options?)    → Promise<HTMLImageElement>
snapdom.toWebp(element, options?)   → Promise<HTMLImageElement>
snapdom.toCanvas(element, options?) → Promise<HTMLCanvasElement>
snapdom.toBlob(element, options?)   → Promise<Blob>
snapdom.download(element, options?) → Promise<void>
snapdom.plugins(...definitions)    → snapdom
snapdom.preCapture()               → void
snapdom.version                    → string
```

Static shortcuts capture and then export. Use `snapdom.toJpg()` for the JPEG shortcut; `result.toJpeg()` is also available on a capture result. `snapdom.toImg()` is a deprecated alias for `snapdom.toSvg()`.

`fromString()` mounts markup offscreen in the live document, lets page CSS and fonts apply, captures it, then removes the mount. A single root element becomes the target; otherwise it captures the wrapper. The markup goes through `innerHTML`: use trusted HTML or sanitize it first. This method requires a browser DOM; it does not render HTML in Node.js.

```js
const capture = await snapdom.fromString('<article class="card">Hello</article>');
const image = await capture.toPng();
```

## CaptureResult

| Member | Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | string | SVG data URL on the SVG engine; lazily encoded PNG after successful native capture |
| `needs` | `'clone'` or `'render'` | Stage reached by this capture |
| `meta` | frozen CaptureMeta | Render geometry; throws below render |
| `warnings` | array | Fallback or degradation records; export-time entries append after export |
| `toRaw()` | string, synchronous | Same URL as `url`; no rasterization on SVG, PNG encoding on first native read |
| `toSvg(options?)` | Promise<HTMLImageElement> | SVG-backed image normally; PNG-backed after successful native capture |
| `toImg(options?)` | Promise<HTMLImageElement> | Deprecated alias for `toSvg()` |
| `toPng(options?)` | Promise<HTMLImageElement> | PNG image |
| `toJpg(options?)`, `toJpeg(options?)` | Promise<HTMLImageElement> | JPEG image |
| `toWebp(options?)` | Promise<HTMLImageElement> | WebP image |
| `toCanvas(options?)` | Promise<HTMLCanvasElement> | Rasterized canvas |
| `toBlob(options?)` | Promise<Blob> | SVG on the SVG engine, PNG on the native engine, unless a format was explicitly selected |
| `download(options?)` | Promise<void> | Triggers a browser download |
| `to(name, options?)` | Promise<any> | Runs a core or plugin export by name |

Examples of plugin helpers are `toHtml()`, `toContext()` and `toAgentMap()`.

### Choosing an engine

Set `engine: 'html-in-canvas'` to request the second integrated engine. It still requires the browser's experimental feature flag or applicable origin trial; supported Chrome builds expose it through `chrome://flags/#canvas-draw-element`. It also needs a build compiled with `SNAPDOM_CANVAS_ENGINE=1 npm run compile`. The default build currently omits it; this is separate from whether the browser exposes `drawElementImage` or its earlier `drawElement` API.

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, { engine: 'html-in-canvas' });
const canvas = await capture.toCanvas();
```

If the engine/API is unavailable, painting fails, or the capture needs unsupported geometry, SnapDOM runs the SVG engine on the same clone. Examples that currently use SVG fallback include capture-level width/height, clipping, transformed ancestors, and plugins with `beforeRender` or `afterRender` hooks.

A successful native capture retains a bitmap. Raster exporters consume it directly; `url` and `toRaw()` encode PNG only when requested. Despite its method name, `toSvg()` returns a PNG-backed image on this path. There is no serialized SVG: `toBlob({ format: 'svg' })` and a plugin's `ctx.export.svgString()` reject. Select `engine: 'svg'` when SVG source is required.

A plugin may request `needs: 'clone'`. If every attached plugin requests that stage, capture stops before rendering. Its structured plugin exports work, but `url`, `meta` and core image exporters throw. Request render when an image is required; a later export does not recapture a clone-only result.

Warnings have the shape `{ code, message, detail? }`. Examples include missing-image fallbacks, canvas size clamps and Safari image fallbacks. Read them after the export when diagnosing output differences.

### Geometry

All `CaptureMeta` dimensions use capture CSS pixels:

```ts
interface CaptureMeta {
  readonly w0: number;        // Logical capture width; clip width when clipped
  readonly h0: number;        // Logical capture height; clip height when clipped
  readonly vbW: number;       // Render viewBox width, including bleed/padding
  readonly vbH: number;       // Render viewBox height, including bleed/padding
  readonly targetW: number;   // Requested output basis before scale/dpr
  readonly targetH: number;
  readonly contentX: number;  // Logical capture origin inside the viewBox
  readonly contentY: number;
  readonly clip: Readonly<{ x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number }> | null;
}
```

Use this metadata for crop placement or overlays instead of reverse-parsing the SVG URL.

### Format selection

`format` is canonical; `type` is a deprecated, synchronized alias. Named helpers choose their own codec. `download()` defaults to PNG. When neither capture nor export explicitly selected a format, `toBlob()` defaults to SVG on the SVG engine and PNG after a successful native capture. This example uses the default SVG engine:

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element);
const svg = await capture.toBlob();
const png = await capture.toBlob({ format: 'png' });
const jpeg = await capture.toBlob({ format: 'jpeg', quality: 0.85 });

const pngCapture = await snapdom(element, { format: 'png' });
const inheritedPng = await pngCapture.toBlob();
```

### Output size and crop

`width` and `height` set the output size before raster `dpr`. One dimension preserves aspect ratio; specifying both can distort it. Either dimension takes precedence over `scale`. When neither is set, `scale` multiplies the captured size. Set `dpr: 1` when an exact raster pixel count matters.

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element);
const image = await capture.toPng({ width: 1200, dpr: 1 });
const canvas = await capture.toCanvas({
  crop: { x: 10, y: 20, width: 300, height: 180 },
  width: 600,
  dpr: 1
});
```

Canvas `crop` is an export window in capture viewBox coordinates. Capture `clip` is a page-coordinate window applied earlier; it can avoid cloning and styling outside subtrees. These coordinate systems are different.

## Capture options

Export methods accept relevant overrides, such as size, background and quality. Options that determine what was captured, such as exclusions and font embedding, belong on `snapdom()`; changing them later cannot rebuild the captured tree.

| Option | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scale: number` | `1` | Output multiplier when neither width nor height is set |
| `dpr: number` | `devicePixelRatio` | Raster density |
| `width`, `height`: number | unset | Absolute output dimensions; win over scale |
| `backgroundColor: string or null` | transparent | JPEG/WebP default to white |
| `quality: number` | `0.92` | JPEG/WebP encoding quality from 0 to 1 |
| `format` | `'png'` | Format-selecting exports; `toBlob()` has the engine-dependent default described above |
| `type` | unset | Deprecated alias for format; accepted values are svg, png, jpg, jpeg, webp |
| `filename: string` | `'snapDOM'` | Download name; adds the format extension if absent |
| `embedFonts: boolean or 'auto'` | `'auto'` | Embed used webfonts; skip system-font-only captures |
| `localFonts: LocalFont[]` | `[]` | Explicit font sources |
| `iconFonts` | `[]` | Additional icon-family string/RegExp matchers, or an array of them |
| `excludeFonts: ExcludeFonts` | unset | Skip non-icon fonts by family, domain or subset |
| `fontStylesheetDomains: string[]` | `[]` | Additional domains allowed for cross-origin font CSS fetching |
| `useProxy: string` | `''` | CORS proxy prefix used as a resource fallback |
| `exclude` | `[]` | Selector, true-to-exclude predicate, or a mixed array |
| `excludeMode` | `'hide'` | Hide keeps layout via an invisible spacer; remove drops the node |
| `excludeStyleProps` | unset | RegExp or predicate selecting computed CSS properties to skip |
| `outerTransforms: boolean` | `true` | Keep root rotation/scale/skew; false removes root rotation while retaining scale/skew; root translation is normalized in either case |
| `outerShadows` | `false` | Strip root shadow/outline/drop-shadow; true keeps them; subtree also bounds descendant shadow ink |
| `clip` | `null` | `'viewport'` or `{ x, y, width, height }` in page coordinates |
| `captureSelection: boolean` | `false` | Include the live text or focused-field selection |
| `fallbackURL` | unset | Fixed image URL or callback receiving measured width/height for failed images |
| `placeholders: boolean` | `true` | Use placeholders for missing resources |
| `canvas: HTMLCanvasElement` | unset | Reuse a raster output target |
| `reconcile: boolean` | `false` | Measure the styled clone and pin boxes that differ from the live layout; adds a layout pass |
| `cache` | `'soft'` | Persistent resource/style cache policy; disabled/false clears and bypasses it; legacy auto/full normalize to soft |
| `invalidate: boolean` | `false` | Force one fresh capture and clear style snapshots after otherwise unobservable changes |
| `plugins: PluginUse[]` | unset | Per-capture plugin definitions; override globals by name |
| `engine` | `'svg'` | Select `'svg'` or experimental `'html-in-canvas'`; native use requires the browser feature and build flag described above |
| `debug: boolean` | `false` | Emit diagnostics through console warnings |

Root `blur()` remains visible and its bleed is included even with `outerShadows: false`. Explicit clip edges do not expand. Descendant transforms remain part of the capture.

### Fonts

`embedFonts: 'auto'` embeds the webfonts used in the subtree. `true` forces the discovery/embed pass; `false` skips text-font embedding and may leave fallback metrics. Icon glyphs use a separate raster path, so they are not controlled by text-font embedding.

```ts
interface LocalFont {
  family: string;
  src: string;
  weight?: string | number;
  style?: string;
  stretchPct?: number; // 100 by default
}

interface ExcludeFonts {
  families?: string[];
  domains?: string[];
  subsets?: string[];
}
```

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  localFonts: [{ family: 'Inter', src: '/fonts/inter.woff2', weight: 400 }]
});
```

Explicit sources avoid remote discovery. Ensure the live layout uses the intended font before capturing; an export cannot repair layout measured with a different font.

### Exclusions and missing assets

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  exclude: ['.export-button', node => node.hasAttribute('data-private')],
  excludeMode: 'remove',
  fallbackURL: ({ width = 300, height = 150 }) =>
    `/image-fallback.svg?width=${width}&height=${height}`
});
```

`data-capture="exclude"` also excludes an element. Core password handling masks password values. Use the `redactInputs` plugin for additional selected fields, private subtrees (`blocks`) and named attributes (`attributes`); see the redaction example below.

For cross-origin resources, configure CORS on the asset server or supply a proxy you control:

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  useProxy: 'https://your-proxy.example/?url='
});
```

Proxying assets gives that service the requested resource URLs. It does not grant access to cross-origin iframe documents.

### Automatic asset sizing

SnapDOM may reduce oversized embedded bitmap assets based on displayed size, transforms and requested raster density. This can reduce SVG payload size and later decoding work. The SVG result retains the original assets for larger subsequent raster exports. A successful native capture is already a bitmap, so larger exports scale its captured pixels. CSS style compression is internal; there is no public compression switch.

## Cache and preCapture

There are three forms of reuse:

1. Exporting an existing `CaptureResult` uses that capture's state.
2. Calling `snapdom()` again may reuse an eligible unchanged memo or differentially recapture supported changes.
3. Persistent caches reuse resource data and style work across captures.

`cache: 'disabled'` or `false` controls the third form. It does not disable automatic repeat memoization. Legacy `cache: 'auto'` and `'full'` are accepted as `'soft'`.

Eligible static captures can be memoized from their first successful capture. DOM, style, font and environment changes observed by the engine invalidate relevant work. Canvas, video and iframe trees capture fresh because their visual contents can change without a DOM mutation. Live selection also requires fresh capture.

Direct stylesheet edits such as `sheet.insertRule()` or `cssRule.style.color = ...` do not emit the DOM mutations used for style invalidation. After such changes, use:

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, { invalidate: true });
```

That call bypasses the previous memo and clears style snapshots. Its stable fresh result may become the memo for later captures.

Arm intent-based preparation once:

```js
snapdom.preCapture();

button.addEventListener('click', async () => {
  const capture = await snapdom(card);
  await capture.download({ filename: 'card.png' });
});
```

An eligible capture started in the same event task as a press, click or Enter/Space activation teaches `preCapture()` which target and top-level options belong to that control. Later pointer-enter, focus or press intent can prefetch it. The options are shallow-copied. An initial unknown pointer/focus intent can warm the viewport once; it cannot yet know an unseen control's target. There are no arguments, declarations or background polling.

`preCache` was removed in v3. There is no `fast` option.

## Plugins

### Registration

```js
import { filter, htmlExport } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';

const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [filter({ preset: 'grayscale' }), htmlExport()]
});
const image = await capture.toPng();
const html = await capture.toHtml();
```

For global registration, use `snapdom.plugins(plugin, ...)`. Definitions may be instances, factories, `[factory, options]` tuples or `{ plugin: factory, options }` objects. Per-capture definitions override global ones with the same `name`. Clone-only plugins must be passed per capture; global plugins cannot lower every capture's stage.

### Official plugin exports

| Factory | Output or effect | Selected options/defaults |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `filter()` | CSS filter on the clone | preset: grayscale, sepia, blur, invert, vintage, dramatic; or a CSS filter string |
| `colorTint()` | Color overlay | color red, opacity 1 |
| `replaceText()` | Text substitutions in the clone | replacements: array of `{ find: string or RegExp, replace: string }` |
| `timestampOverlay()` | Timestamp badge | format datetime, position bottom-right |
| `redactInputs()` | Masks input/textarea values, excludes blocks and removes named attributes | types, autocomplete, selector, all, mask, blocks, attributes |
| `asciiExport()` | `toAscii()` → string | width 80 characters, charset `' .:-=+*#%@'`, invert false |
| `pdfImage()` | `toPdfImage()` → object URL, also downloads | portrait A4, JPEG quality 0.92, filename capture.pdf |
| `htmlExport()` | `toHtml()` → string | fullDocument true, filename capture.html |
| `contextExport()` | `toContext()` → outline string or JSON | format outline, geometry true, maxTextLength 120, maxNodes 800 |
| `agentMap()` | `toAgentMap()` → object | image annotated, fields minimal, semantic false, maxImageWidth 1024 |
| `gifExport()` | `toGif()` → Blob | fps 10, duration 2000 ms, frames overrides duration |
| `videoExport()` | `toMp4()` → Blob | fps 10, duration 2000 ms, frames overrides duration |

The MIT `pdfImage` plugin puts a JPEG on a single page with margins. It does not provide selectable text or semantic pagination, and `toPdfImage()` is not a Blob-returning API.

### Redaction across outputs

```js
import { redactInputs, htmlExport, contextExport } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';

const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [
    redactInputs({
      all: true,
      blocks: ['.private-panel', '[data-private-block]'],
      attributes: [
        { selector: '[data-token]', names: ['data-token'] },
        { selector: '.customer', names: ['title', 'aria-label'] }
      ]
    }),
    htmlExport(),
    contextExport({ format: 'json' })
  ]
});
const image = await capture.toPng();
const html = await capture.toHtml();
const context = await capture.toContext();
```

The live page stays unchanged. Field selection uses `types` (default email/tel), `autocomplete` (default cc-*, current-password, new-password, one-time-code), an extra `selector`, or `all: true`. `selector` applies only to inputs and textareas; use `blocks` for other elements. The default mask replaces values with same-length bullets; custom `mask(value, element)` can return another string. Glyph widths can differ, so wrapping can change.

`blocks` accepts a CSS selector or an array and combines with `exclude`. It preserves invisible space by default; `excludeMode: 'remove'` removes the subtree from layout. Removing a blocked capture root throws; use `'hide'` for that capture. Selectors match source elements, including nodes in open shadow trees.

`attributes` accepts `{ selector: string, names: string[] }` rules. Each rule removes exact named attributes and their projections in agent maps and context; names are not wildcard patterns. A `value` rule on an input or textarea clears its displayed value and omits structured `state.value`. Attribute removal does not erase copies in visible text, CSS `content` or bitmap pixels; use `blocks` for the subtree that paints that content. The rules do not search arbitrary text or images for sensitive information.

HTML uses the sanitized clone. `agentMap` and `contextExport` share the field, block and attribute policy for source-derived data, regardless of official plugin order. Existing default field masks still apply when you add block or attribute rules.

Custom masks and nonempty `selector`, `blocks` or `attributes` rules disable unchanged-capture memoization, so they run on every capture. Nonempty block or attribute rules add a final `beforeRender` pass; the experimental `engine: 'html-in-canvas'` then falls back to SVG. Field-only redaction does not add that pass. Full plugin options: https://github.com/zumerlab/snapdom/blob/main/packages/plugins/README.md#redact-inputs.

### SnapDOM Pro previews

SnapDOM Pro contains paid plugin previews for searchable PDF export and editable vector SVG export. These are separate from the MIT core and `@zumer/snapdom-plugins`; neither is included in the official plugin exports listed above. The preview pages document sample output and current limits. The current previews target SnapDOM 3.0.0-beta.0 or later; consult each product's documentation for supported versions and release status.

- Pro overview: https://snapdom.dev/pro/
- PDF preview and samples: https://snapdom.dev/pro/pdf/
- PDF documentation: https://snapdom.dev/pro/pdf/docs.html
- Vector preview and samples: https://snapdom.dev/pro/vector/
- Vector documentation: https://snapdom.dev/pro/vector/docs.html

### HTML and structured context

```js
import { htmlExport, contextExport } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';

const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [htmlExport(), contextExport()]
});
const documentHtml = await capture.toHtml();
const fragment = await capture.toHtml({ fullDocument: false });
const outline = await capture.toContext();
const tree = await capture.toContext({ format: 'json' });
```

HTML output contains the captured markup, styles and assets. It preserves source event-handler attributes; treat it as untrusted when serving it. It is not a sanitizer. `toHtml({ download: true })` also downloads; a string value for `download` supplies the filename.

Context JSON has `{ root, truncated, nodes }`. Each node may contain `tag`, `id`, `class`, `box`, `text`, `state` and nested `children`. Text and node caps can truncate output. It describes the captured tree; it does not provide interaction commands.

For context alone, skip the render stage:

```js
const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [contextExport({ needs: 'clone', format: 'json' })]
});
const tree = await capture.toContext();
```

### Annotated maps

```js
import { agentMap } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';

const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [agentMap({ image: 'annotated', fields: 'full' })]
});
const annotated = await capture.toAgentMap();
const raw = await capture.toAgentMap({ image: 'raw' });
```

The result shape is `{ dimensions: { width, height }, map, image? }`. `image`, when requested, is a data URL. Each map entry uses these keys:

- `i`: numeric label id
- `n`: accessible name or text label
- `r`: role
- `b`: bounding box array `[x, y, width, height]`
- Interactive entries may add `s` (state). Full fields may add `t` (text) and `a` (attributes). Semantic entries carry `isSemanticOnly`.

The image and map refer to the same captured state. `image: 'raw'` omits labels; `image: false` omits the image. `semantic: true` adds non-interactive semantic elements. `maxImageWidth`, `imageFormat` (png/jpg/webp), `imageQuality`, selectors and `labelStyle` customize the output. For map-only capture, use `{ image: false, needs: 'clone' }`.

Boxes account for capture geometry, but complex transformed ancestors and perspective can limit alignment. Maps are capture data, not a browser automation or action-verification API. Comparing capture URLs only compares serialized output; it does not establish that an interaction succeeded.

### Recordings

```js
import { gifExport, videoExport } from '@zumer/snapdom-plugins';

const capture = await snapdom(element, {
  plugins: [gifExport({ fps: 10, duration: 2000 }), videoExport({ fps: 10 })]
});
const gif = await capture.toGif();
const video = await capture.toMp4();
console.log(video.type); // Actual MP4 or WebM container
```

Recording starts at export time and captures the live element repeatedly, including its first frame. Capture policies such as exclusions continue to apply. An explicit `frames` count overrides `duration`; scale inherits the original capture unless supplied. The video plugin needs `MediaRecorder` and canvas `captureStream()`, and falls back to WebM when MP4 is unavailable. Check `blob.type` when naming or serving the result. Either recording export accepts `download: true` or a filename string.

### Plugin lifecycle

Capture hooks run in registration order:

```text
beforeSnap → beforeClone → resolveNode (per node) → afterClone
→ beforeRender → afterRender → defineExports
→ [beforeExport → exporter → afterExport] for each export
→ afterSnap once, after the first successful export
```

Clone-only captures stop before the render hooks. All hooks can be async. Core exclusions are checked before `resolveNode()`: return a replacement `Node`, `null` to skip, or `undefined` for normal cloning. The first plugin that returns a value wins for that node.

Capture hooks share a context with normalized options at the top level, such as `ctx.scale`, and `ctx.options` refers to that capture context. `beforeSnap` can change those options, except `plugins`, `needs`, `invalidate` and `cache`, which have already been resolved.

`ctx.clone` is available from `afterClone` through `afterRender`, then released. In `afterRender`, copy any serialized data needed later. Keep per-capture state on that capture's context or in the closure created by `defineExports`; shared mutable plugin-factory state can mix separate captures.

Export hooks receive a per-export context view and a payload. `payload.options` is the same merged options object the exporter receives; mutate it in `beforeExport` to change the export. `ctx.export.requestedOptions` preserves the exact explicit overrides. `ctx.export.url` is the capture URL, and `ctx.export.svgString()` lazily reads SVG text when the capture has it; it rejects for a native bitmap. Both `beforeExport` and `afterExport` return values are ignored; `afterExport` cannot replace the result.

Declare a custom exporter to produce another result. Capture the core facade during `defineExports`; its methods bypass hooks, avoiding recursive export calls:

```js
const imageBundle = {
  name: 'image-bundle',
  defineExports({ exports: core, meta }) {
    return {
      bundle: async (_context, options) => ({
        image: (await core.png(options)).src,
        width: meta.w0,
        height: meta.h0
      })
    };
  }
};

const capture = await snapdom(element, { plugins: [imageBundle] });
const bundle = await capture.toBundle();
```

The key `bundle` creates both `result.toBundle(options)` and `result.to('bundle', options)`. Using the core facade preserves its geometry, asset-resolution and browser handling. Do not assume `ctx.exports` exists later inside the exporter; retain the facade from `defineExports` as above. Return fresh mutable output objects so one caller cannot corrupt later exports.

Capture-affecting hooks disable automatic memo reuse unless the plugin declares `pure: true`. Use that declaration only for deterministic, idempotent hooks. Pure render hooks can use differential recapture; clone-construction hooks still need a full recapture after a change. Clone-only captures are not memoized. Time-dependent plugins should not claim purity.

## Migration notes

- Replace `preCache()` with normal capture reuse and optional no-argument `preCapture()`.
- Remove `fast`; v3 uses automatic memoization and internal optimizations.
- Replace removed capture `filter`/`filterMode` with `exclude`/`excludeMode`. Invert old keep predicates: `filter: keep` becomes `exclude: node => !keep(node)`. This does not affect the separate CSS-effect plugin named `filter`.
- `embedFonts` defaults to `'auto'`.
- Width or height wins over scale across exporters.
- Prefer canonical `format` to deprecated `type`.
- `afterExport` observes a result; use `defineExports` to return another format or shape.
- Stage names are `clone` and `render`; the old `dom` stage is removed.
- `prompt-export` was renamed to `agent-map`; use `toAgentMap()` and its compact `map` schema.
- Video export is named `toMp4()`, with possible WebM fallback, not `toVideo()`.

## Browser boundaries and troubleshooting

SnapDOM needs a real browser DOM. It captures an existing interface; it does not navigate to arbitrary URLs or automate user actions. Use a browser automation tool for those tasks. Test output in the browsers and viewers you support.

SVG output contains HTML inside `foreignObject`; it is not a set of editable native SVG paths. Some image viewers do not support that content. Use PNG/JPEG/WebP when the destination cannot display it.

Open Shadow DOM and same-origin iframe contents can be captured. Closed shadow roots and cross-origin iframe documents are inaccessible. Tainted canvases, inaccessible images, external fonts and browser raster limits can require fallbacks. An iframe placeholder or partial asset fallback is not a capture of inaccessible content.

If output differs, read `capture.warnings` after export, use `debug: true`, and check the affected resource, font and capture dimensions. Verify the source is laid out with its final styles before capture. A missing webfont changes measurements; inaccessible assets can produce placeholders; oversized output can be clamped. `reconcile: true` adds clone measurement when layout diverges. Do not discard CSS properties or disable font embedding merely to hide a fidelity problem.
